description: Maximum feed request latency observed at the container, across all operation types and clusters.
Total feed operation rate (puts, updates, removes) handled by container clusters, summed across operation types.
Average commit latency (time to commit fed changes to the index/store) on content nodes.
Rate of commit operations (batched writes applied to the index/store) on content nodes.
Rate of PUT operations processed by the storage/persistence-engine layer on content nodes, counted per document replica.
Maximum PUT operation latency observed at the storage/persistence-engine layer on content nodes.
Average UPDATE operation latency at the storage/persistence-engine layer on content nodes.

Maximum put operation latency observed at the distributor level.

Maximum visitor operation latency observed at the distributor level.

Rate of failed put operations at the distributor level; non-zero values indicate issues with writes.

Average document processing (docproc chain) latency.
Rate of documents processed through document processing (docproc) chains, summed across all chains and clusters.
Number of content nodes currently exceeding a resource usage limit; when greater than zero, feeding is blocked for that cluster.
Average feed latency, in milliseconds, for successful feed operations.
Rate of PUT operations received via the Document/HTTP API.
Average latency of Document/HTTP API requests, distinct from the generic jdisc HTTP layer latency.
Maximum number of Document/HTTP API requests pending (in-flight, not yet completed) on the container.
Rate of failed Document/HTTP API operations.
Average end-to-end HTTP write request latency at the container's HTTP layer.

Maximum number of documents held in the in-memory index on content nodes, summed per content group (to combine per-node/stripe values) and maxed across groups (since each group holds a full replica) to avoid double-counting.
Average depth of the per-node persistence engine's input operation queue (operations waiting to be dispatched to Proton) over the time window.
Maximum number of concurrently active (in-flight) operations in the content node's persistence engine.
